title: Signal-to-Provision Playbook: Mapping Emerging Model Capabilities to Capacity Commitments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook that translates continuous model-landscape signals (availability, latency, cost, licensing risk, accuracy deltas) into concrete procurement and Dedicated capacity decisions. Aim is to reduce reactive spend by providing engineering and procurement with clearly defined trigger thresholds, experiment buckets (canary/prod split), and fallbacks for model substitutions. Deliverables: scenario matrix, telemetry queries, templated procurement ask, rollout checklist, and a small eval harness to flag quality regressions before commits.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario matrix covering at least three verticals (search, embeddings, chat) mapping 6 signal types to procurement actions
Telemetry queries and dashboard links that surface the triggers (p50/p95 latency, cost-per-1k-tokens, embedding recall delta)
Procurement ask template with cost delta estimates and commitment / cancellation clauses for Dedicated capacity
A canary rollout checklist and automated gating rules integrated into Console release flows
A 5-run eval harness and sample prompt set for each vertical to detect quality regressions on model swap
tasks: Catalog candidate external models and variant families with licensing notes and region availability
Define signal taxonomy and instrumentation for each signal type (availability, latency, cost, accuracy, quantization risk, vendor SLAs)
Run 3 procurement-scenario simulations using historical traffic slices to estimate cost and latency impact
Produce procurement template and triage matrix for legal/procurement review
Prototype a Console gating rule that uses Datadog/Prometheus query to block full commit until canary metrics pass
Ship eval harness + shared prompt sets to surv-evals for continuous monitoring
